title: Regular divisor under etale base change
statement: Let φ:R→S be a ring homomorphism whose map of affine schemes is etale. Suppose R is regular, multiplication by g on R is injective, and R/(g) is regular. Then S is regular, multiplication by φ(g) on S is injective, and S/(φ(g)) is regular.

proof.text:
An etale ring map is flat, so tensoring the injective multiplication map by g
preserves injectivity; this gives regular multiplication by its image. Regularity
ascends under etale ring maps. The quotient S/(φ(g)) is the base change of S along
R to R/(g); it is etale over that regular quotient, so it too is regular. This applies
also when g is a unit, in which case both quotients are the zero ring.

    (R S : CommRingCat.{u}) (φ : R →+* S)
    [IsRegularRing R] (g : R) (hg : IsSMulRegular R g)
    [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {g})]

      IsRegularRing (S ⧸ Ideal.span {φ g})
